facts.statement: The genus name Lucianovenator means "Luciano's hunter" and honors Don Luciano Leyes, who first reported the fossil remains.
facts.quote: The genus name Lucianovenator translates to "Luciano's hunter", in reference to Don Luciano Leyes, who first reported the remains.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen PVSJ 906 was discovered in the Quebrada del Puma locality within the Quebrada del Barro Formation in Argentina.
facts.quote: The holotype (PVSJ 906) of Lucianovenator bonoi was found in the "Quebrada del puma" locality of the Quebrada del Barro Formation in Argentina

facts.statement: The holotype consists of an articulated sequence of vertebrae from the third cervical to the fourth dorsal, along with a sacrum and a partial pelvis.
facts.quote: PVSJ 906 represents an articulated vertebral sequence from the third cervical to fourth dorsal vertebra, as well as a sacrum and a partial pelvis.

facts.statement: Three additional specimens (PVSJ 899, PVSJ 1013, and PVSJ 1084) have been referred to the species, consisting mainly of sacra and partial pelves.
facts.quote: In addition, three more specimens were referred to Lucianovenator. These include PVSJ 899 (a sacrum and partial pelvis), PVSJ 1013 (a sacrum), and PVSJ 1084 (a sacrum and partial pelvis).

facts.statement: A proximal right tibia (PVSJ 1004) is tentatively attributed to the species.
facts.quote: PVSJ 1004, the proximal end of a right tibia, may also belong to the species.

facts.statement: The holotype was discovered in 2014 by paleontologist Ricardo N. Martínez and his team at the Universidad Nacional de San Juan.
facts.quote: El espécimen holotipo, PVSJ 906, de Lucianovenator bonoi fue hallado en la localidad "Quebrada del Puma" en la Formación Quebrada del Barro en Argentina, descubierta en el año 2014 por el paleontólogo de la Universidad Nacional de San Juan Ricardo N. Martínez y su equipo.

facts.statement: Lucianovenator is an extinct coelophysoid theropod dinosaur that lived in Argentina during the Triassic period.
facts.quote: Lucianovenator is an extinct genus of coelophysoid theropod dinosaur which lived in Argentina during the Triassic.

facts.statement: The fossils date to the late Norian to Rhaetian stages, approximately 210 to 202 million years ago.
facts.quote: which is estimated to be from the late Norian to Rhaetian in age, approximately 210 to 202 million years ago.

facts.statement: Lucianovenator is one of the few known neotheropod dinosaurs from South America.
facts.quote: It is one of the few neotheropods known from South America.

facts.statement: An initial phylogenetic analysis placed Lucianovenator in the family Coelophysidae alongside Coelophysis rhodesiensis and Camposaurus.
facts.quote: A phylogenetic analysis published along with the description of Lucianovenator assigned it to the Coelophysidae, in a clade with Coelophyis rhodesiensis and Camposaurus.

facts.statement: Later phylogenetic studies recovered Lucianovenator as a coelophysoid that is not a member of the Coelophysidae family.
facts.quote: Subsequent phylogenetic analyses recovered Lucianovenator as a non-coelophysid coelophysoid.

facts.statement: Lucianovenator can be distinguished from other neotheropods by a unique combination of four specific pairs of paired pits on its cervical vertebrae.
facts.quote: Although the cervicals of Lucianovenator possess many fossae, four particular examples of paired fossae (four on each side of the vertebrae) can be used to distinguish it from other neotheropods.

facts.statement: The anterior cervical ribs of Lucianovenator are exceptionally long, measuring more than five times the length of the cervical vertebrae.
facts.quote: Another of Lucianovenator's distinguishing traits is that the anterior cervical ribs are very long (more than five times as long as the cervical centra).

facts.statement: Lucianovenator possesses a unique autapomorphy where the edge of each centrodiapophyseal lamina develops a long, deep pit that grows progressively longer and deeper toward the base of the neck.
facts.quote: Lucianovenator is unique in the fact that the edge of each centrodiapophyseal lamina (which connects each diapophysis to the centrum) acquires a long and deep pit, which becomes progressively longer and deeper towards the base of the neck.

facts.statement: The initial clade grouping Lucianovenator with other dinosaurs was supported by the single feature of fused sacral zygapophyses.
facts.quote: Este clado está respaldado por una sola característica, el hecho de que las cigófitas de las vértebras sacras están fusionadas.

facts.statement: The genus Lucianovenator was named by Martinez and Apaldetti in 2017.
facts.quote: PBDB name: Lucianovenator (genus), Martinez and Apaldetti 2017

Lucianovenator lived during the Norian stage of the Triassic, between 227.3 and 205.7 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Norian to Norian (227.3 to 205.7 million years ago)

facts.statement: There is currently only one recorded fossil occurrence of Lucianovenator.
